## What's new

### Files: browse and edit your code
A new **Files** view shows the project tree with a built-in editor: syntax highlighting for PHP, Blade, JS/TS, Vue, CSS, JSON, YAML, Markdown and more, plus search (⌘F), folding, multiple cursors and ⌘S to save.
- Unsaved edits survive switching views.
- A save is refused if the file changed on disk in the meantime, so nothing gets overwritten silently.
- Binary and very large files open in your own editor instead.

### Fuzzy file finder
Press **⌘P** (Ctrl+P on Windows and Linux) in Files to jump to any file by typing parts of its name or path. It lists what git tracks, plus new files that aren't ignored, and skips `vendor` and `node_modules`.

### Remove a project from anywhere
Hover the project name at the top of the sidebar to find a trash button. Before, you could only remove a project from Overview. It asks first, and your files are never touched.

## Fixes
- **Dev servers kept running after you stopped them** (macOS and Linux). Stopping the stack, closing a terminal or quitting Larvyn stopped `npm run dev` and `artisan serve`, but left vite and the PHP server running in the background. That kept ports busy and gave "port already in use" on the next start. Larvyn now stops the whole process tree, including anything you started from a shell tab.
- **"code was not found on PATH" on macOS.** Open in editor now also finds VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, PhpStorm and Sublime Text inside their apps in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`, even if you never installed their command-line tool. When an editor really isn't installed, the message says how to set it up.
- **Quitting is faster** with many terminals open: they're stopped in parallel.

## Under the hood
The Go backend is being split into `internal/` packages (store, proc, updater, git, terminal). Nothing changes for you, but it makes the code easier to work on.
